issue.what: IMF package structure is incomplete or inconsistent.
issue.why: IMF is atomic — a broken track/metadata can cause the whole package to be rejected.
issue.fix: Ensure ASSETMAP/PKL/CPL and MXF assets are complete and consistent, then re-wrap/rebuild the IMF.

issue.what: Language/metadata in the IMF does not match the delivery request.
issue.why: A mismatch can block delivery ingestion.
issue.fix: Set the correct language code and rebuild/re-wrap the IMF package.

issue.what: Dolby Vision metadata looks abnormal or DV XML is missing.
issue.why: Incorrect DV metadata often triggers redelivery or a fix request.
issue.fix: Verify DV XML/CMVersion in mastering and export/re-wrap again.

issue.what: Audio is not uncompressed PCM WAV/BWAV.
issue.why: Delivery audio should be uncompressed WAV/BWAV for compatibility and QC.
issue.fix: Re-export as PCM WAV/BWAV and replace the file.

issue.what: Sample rate is not 48 kHz.
issue.why: Nearfield/print masters typically require 48 kHz.
issue.fix: Re-export at 48 kHz PCM WAV/BWAV and replace the file.

issue.what: Channel count/layout does not match what’s expected.
issue.why: Wrong channel layout can break QC and downstream mixing.
issue.fix: Check routing/export preset and re-export.

issue.what: Cannot auto-verify embedded audio in this build.
issue.why: Missing embedded audio can break review/encoding workflows.
issue.fix: Confirm audio is embedded, or re-export with embedded audio and replace the file.

issue.what: Cannot auto-detect variable frame rate (VFR) in this build.
issue.why: VFR can cause sync and QC issues.
issue.fix: Confirm it is constant frame rate (CFR), or re-export/convert to CFR.

issue.what: Detailed codec/container validation requires external tools.
issue.why: This is a common source of delivery failures.
issue.fix: Export using the team’s approved preset.

issue.what: Cannot auto-verify ProRes 422 HQ profile in this build.
issue.why: Servicing turnover must match the required ProRes profile.
issue.fix: Confirm from export preset (or attach MediaInfo), then mark as confirmed.

issue.what: Please confirm this is Textless Complete.
issue.why: Textless deliverables must not include burned-in subtitles/unwanted graphics.
issue.fix: Tick the checklist items after verifying playback.

issue.what: checksum.txt is missing.
issue.why: Archive deliveries rely on checksums to verify integrity.
issue.fix: Generate checksum.txt for the sequence folder and add it to the package.

issue.what: File path length is longer than recommended.
issue.why: Overly long paths can break transfers and automated tools.
issue.fix: Shorten folder/file names to reduce the maximum path length.

issue.what: Potentially illegal characters found in file/folder names.
issue.why: Some systems fail ingest when names contain special characters.
issue.fix: Rename using safe characters (a–z, 0–9, underscore, dash).

issue.what: ZIP packaging detected (or likely).
issue.why: Some archive workflows prefer raw folders over ZIP.
issue.fix: Deliver as a folder-based sequence + checksum following the agreed structure.

issue.what: Cannot auto-verify global upscale in this build.
issue.why: Archive masters should not be globally upscaled just to reach UHD.
issue.fix: Confirm the true source resolution and provide proof/exception if needed.

issue.what: One or more files are empty (0 bytes).
issue.why: Zero-byte files indicate a failed export, interrupted copy, or placeholder stub. Any downstream tool that tries to parse or ingest them will fail.
issue.fix: Delete the empty file(s) and re-export or re-copy the originals. If this is a placeholder, replace it with the real file before running preflight again.

issue.what: Required files have not been added.
issue.why: Missing files block downstream QC and handoff.
issue.fix: Add the missing files/folders and run preflight again.

issue.what: Folder structure does not look shot-based.
issue.why: Shot-based structure makes QC and retrieval faster.
issue.fix: Organize as /SHOW/EP/SHOT/... then deliver again.

issue.what: ZIP file detected.
issue.why: Some VFX/archive paths discourage ZIP packaging.
issue.fix: Deliver using folders following the agreed structure.

issue.what: CPL references track files that are not declared in PKL and/or ASSETMAP.
issue.why: IMF ingest/QC expects every MXF referenced by the CPL to be declared in the manifest. Missing declarations commonly cause package rejection or redelivery.
issue.fix: Rebuild/re-export the IMF so PKL and ASSETMAP include every MXF referenced by the CPL (including IAB). Avoid copying MXFs into an IMP without regenerating PKL/ASSETMAP.

issue.what: ASSETMAP references files that are missing from the package.
issue.why: IMF ingest/QC relies on ASSETMAP paths to locate assets. Missing paths commonly cause ingest failure or redelivery.
issue.fix: Ensure all referenced MXF/XML files exist in the IMP folder, then regenerate ASSETMAP/PKL by re-exporting/repackaging the IMF.

issue.what: One or more assets declared in the PKL are missing or do not match the actual file size.
issue.why: PKL is used for package integrity. Size mismatches often indicate incomplete copy/corruption and can cause rejection.
issue.fix: Re-copy assets without interruption, or re-export/repackage to regenerate PKL/ASSETMAP. Avoid modifying/copying assets after PKL creation.

issue.what: ASSETMAP and PKL do not declare the same set of assets (excluding the PKL file itself).
issue.why: ASSETMAP and PKL are the authoritative manifests for locating and validating assets. A mismatch usually indicates an incomplete/stale package and may cause ingest/QC failure.
issue.fix: Re-export/repackage the IMF so ASSETMAP and PKL are regenerated together. Avoid copying/replacing assets after manifest creation.

issue.what: One or more PKL hashes do not match the actual file contents (or cannot be verified).
issue.why: PKL hashes are used to validate package integrity. A hash mismatch often indicates corruption or a wrong/partial file and can cause rejection.
issue.fix: Re-copy assets without interruption or re-export/repackage to regenerate PKL/ASSETMAP. Avoid modifying/copying assets after PKL creation.

IMF_CPL_PKL_HASH_MATCH.title: CPL hash matches PKL hash (manifest consistency)

issue.what: CPL Hash for one or more TrackFileIds does not match the corresponding PKL hash (or hashing metadata is inconsistent).
issue.why: CPL/PKL hash mismatches usually indicate a stale/edited manifest or swapped/corrupted assets and can trigger IMF ingest/QC rejection.
issue.fix: Re-export/repackage the IMF so CPL/PKL/ASSETMAP are regenerated together. Avoid copying/replacing MXF assets after manifest creation.

issue.what: One or more IMF IDs are not valid UUIDs or are duplicated inside a manifest.
issue.why: IMF uses UUIDs to reference assets. Invalid/duplicate IDs can break manifest resolution and ingest.
issue.fix: Re-export/repackage the IMF using a conforming tool. Avoid hand-editing IDs.

issue.what: One or more assets declared in ASSETMAP do not match the actual file size (Length) or cannot be resolved.
issue.why: ASSETMAP Length is part of package integrity. A mismatch often indicates an incomplete copy, corruption, or a stale manifest and can cause ingest/QC failure.
issue.fix: Re-copy assets without interruption, or re-export/repackage to regenerate ASSETMAP/PKL. Avoid modifying/copying assets after manifest creation.

IMF_CPL_TIMELINE_INTEGRITY.title: CPL timeline integrity (resource bounds / duration sync)

issue.what: CPL contains invalid resource trims (EntryPoint/SourceDuration out of bounds) and/or sequence durations are out of sync.
issue.why: Invalid CPL timing can break playback/merge and commonly triggers ingest/QC rejection.
issue.fix: Re-export/repackage the IMF and ensure all tracks are aligned in duration. Avoid hand-editing CPL timing values.

issue.what: One or more MXF files do not appear to be valid MXF (bad header UL) or are unusually small.
issue.why: Invalid/corrupted MXF assets can break IMF playback/merge and commonly trigger ingest/QC rejection.
issue.fix: Re-copy/re-export/repackage the MXF assets. Avoid renaming or replacing MXF files after creating PKL/ASSETMAP.

IMF_MXF_PARTITION_PACK_SANITY.title: MXF partition pack sanity (Header Partition Pack)

issue.what: One or more MXF files are missing a valid Header Partition Pack or have invalid header byte count.
issue.why: Partition Pack / header metadata issues can indicate corruption or non-conformant MXF and may trigger ingest/QC rejection.
issue.fix: Re-export/re-wrap the MXF track files. Avoid copying/replacing MXF files after PKL/ASSETMAP generation.

IMF_MXF_ESSENCE_CONTAINER_LABELS.title: MXF essence container label vs CPL sequence (JPEG2000 / IAB)

issue.what: Essence Container Labels in MXF do not match expected type for CPL sequences (e.g., ImageSequence expects JPEG2000, IABSequence expects IAB).
issue.why: A mismatch often indicates wrong essence mapping or a stale/incorrect export and can lead to ingest/QC failure.
issue.fix: Verify the MXF track file mapping/export settings (JPEG2000 for picture, correct IAB mapping for immersive audio), then re-wrap/re-export.

IMF_CPL_STRUCTURAL_SANITY.title: CPL structural sanity (required sequences / TrackId / EditRate)

issue.what: CPL structure is invalid or inconsistent (missing Segment/Sequence/TrackId/Resource fields, duplicate IDs, or EditRate mismatch).
issue.why: Structural issues can break IMF playback/merge and commonly trigger ingest/QC rejection.
issue.fix: Re-export/repackage the IMF so the CPL is regenerated correctly (do not hand-edit CPL XML). Ensure EditRate/timebase is consistent across all resources.

issue.what: CompositionTimecode is missing or looks abnormal (rate/start address).
issue.why: Incorrect composition timecode can cause timeline/TC mismatch in downstream systems and may lead to redelivery.
issue.fix: Verify CPL CompositionTimecode (rate/drop-frame/start address) matches the intended timeline and re-export/repackage the IMF if needed.

IMF_MXF_DESCRIPTOR_REQUIRED_FIELDS.title: MXF header metadata: required descriptor fields

issue.what: One or more MXF track files are missing key descriptor metadata (e.g., StoredWidth/StoredHeight for picture, AudioSamplingRate/ChannelCount for audio) or header metadata could not be read.
issue.why: Missing/invalid descriptor metadata is a common cause of IMF ingest/QC rejection or downstream mapping errors.
issue.fix: Re-wrap/re-export the IMF MXF track files (do not hand-edit MXF). Ensure your IMF encoder writes correct MXF descriptor metadata, then regenerate PKL/ASSETMAP.

issue.what: Picture MXF track files in the IMF use inconsistent stored frame sizes (resolution).
issue.why: Mixed resolutions inside a single IMF composition often fail ingest/QC and can break downstream conform/merge.
issue.fix: Re-export/re-wrap picture track files so all ImageSequence track files use the same intended resolution, then regenerate PKL/ASSETMAP.

IMF_MXF_AUDIO_SAMPLERATE_48K.title: MXF audio sampling rate must be 48 kHz

issue.what: One or more audio MXF track files declare an AudioSamplingRate that is not 48 kHz.
issue.why: IMF audio is typically required to be 48 kHz for delivery; a mismatch is a frequent hard reject.
issue.fix: Re-export/re-wrap the audio track files at 48 kHz and rebuild the IMF package (regenerate PKL/ASSETMAP).

IMF_MXF_SAMPLERATE_MATCH_CPL.title: MXF descriptor SampleRate matches CPL EditRate

issue.what: One or more MXF track files declare a descriptor SampleRate that does not match the CPL Resource EditRate.
issue.why: A mismatch can indicate incorrect wrapping/timebase and may cause ingest/QC failure or timeline drift.
issue.fix: Re-wrap/re-export track files with the correct timebase (SampleRate) matching the intended CPL EditRate, then regenerate CPL/PKL/ASSETMAP.
